children: November 17 (Renewables Now) - Indian solar manufacturer Vikram Solar Ltd (BOM:544488) on Monday reported a 95.4% year-over-year drop in net profit for its second fiscal quarter through September, which the company described as a transition quarter.
Net profit in the period fell to INR 59 million (USD 637,000/EUR 579,000), while revenue from operations slipped 2.9% to INR 10.77 billion and EBITDA margin declined to 9.4% from 21.2% a year ago.

Sales volumes amounted to 591 MW, down 41.2% sequentially and 24.6% from the same quarter of the previous financial year. The company said this reflected the monsoon and deferred execution, while, in terms of costs, it added its modules are still built on bought-in cells. Vikram Solar’s 9-GW N-type TOPCon cell facility at Gangaikondan, Tamil Nadu is on track to produce its first cells in December, with the full capacity to be commissioned in phases.
The company also plans to establish 9 GW of ingot and wafer capacity at the same Gangaikondan site by the 2029 financial year.

Vikram Solar said that during the quarter it made progress in improving the quality of its business mix, strengthening order inflow and advancing backward integration. The share of domestic content requirement (DCR) modules increased to 22% from 7.5% in the preceding quarter, absolute EBITDA per watt improved by 37% sequentially and the company also highlighted the addition of 1.7 GW of new orders during the quarter, compared to 0.8 GW in the first fiscal quarter.

“Our focus for H2 is clear: convert executable orders, improve asset utilisation, deliver increased DCR volumes and commission the cell project in a disciplined manner,” said Chairman and Managing Director Gyanesh Chaudhary.
In the half-year period, net profit fell over 90% to about INR 260 million, while revenue from operations increased 17.7% year-over-year to INR 26.41 billion.

title: Vikram Solar's Q2 profit falls 95%, cell plant on track
